**Line 36 (buffer stays at 64 MB) is not a deferral.** It is a decision made inside the task: no work was skipped, and the trigger is a health-log condition. I'm leaving it out of the backlog.

The environment reports this directory as not a git repository, even though the session names the branch `feat/upload-retry`. If that is right, `git mv` and `git commit` will fail. I would then use plain `mv` for the same moves and skip the commits, and tell you so.

**Message to my partner:**

Your scan caught a real inconsistency. The plan's Scope section defers payload compression to a future plan, but I had stamped the plan "nothing deferred". I changed the status header to point at `specs/deferred_items.md` and added one backlog item under `## 12-station-upload-retry — 2026-10-30`. It is sized `plan`, with the closure condition "uploads are compressed end to end and the gateway-side tests pass". I recorded the winter-deployment motivation. Tell me if the size or closure condition is wrong.

I did not log the 64 MB buffer line. It is a decision with a trigger (`BUFFER_FULL` in a station's health log), not skipped work, and the closure rubric treats no-action decisions as not needing a checkbox. If you want it watched, I would add it as a `Size: quick-fix` item with `Revisit if: a station health log reports BUFFER_FULL`.

The backlog summary I reported earlier was 7 open, no aged tail. It becomes 8 open with this item, still with no aged tail and under the triage threshold, so no triage is needed.

The retirement is two commits: the deferral record, then `chore(specs): retire plan 12`, which moves both the plan and the spec to their `completed/` folders. Nothing else changes.
